forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West of England Joint Committee has used up its general reserves; budget needs Combined Authority subsidy
news_drafts.lead:
The West of England Joint Committee has no general reserves left, and its budget now balances only with a subsidy from the West of England Combined Authority, according to a report to the joint meeting of the two bodies on 23 October 2026. A combined authority is a body run by several councils together, often with a mayor, for transport and economic growth. General reserves are money put aside as a cushion for the unexpected.

The report, Item 08 on the Joint Committee's budget and change requests, sets this out in its risk section. It says the matter "links to the ongoing reducing general reserves position, which is now exhausted and requires a subsidy from the Combined Authority to balance". The wording describes reserves that had been falling over time and have now run out.

The papers available for this item give no figure for the size of the subsidy, the amount of reserves at an earlier date, or the period the budget covers. They do not say what the Combined Authority has agreed to provide or when.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 09 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast
findings.headline: Investment Fund expenditure £5.9m (20%) below budget with major projects reprofiled: Spatial Development Strategy (£1.8m) and West Rapid Transport (£1.5m) moving costs to future years
findings.detail: Investment Fund Q1 forecast shows £23.4m against budget £29.3m, reduction of £5.9m (20%). Primarily reflects reprofiling of projects into later years. Spatial Development Strategy moving £1.8m (using grant funding before Investment Funding). West Rapid Transport moving £1.5m (lower revenue required as project transitions to capital). Largest planned spend areas: Operations £7.4m, Place £5.8m, Strategic Partnership £4.6m.
findings.matters: Significant project reprofiling indicates slippage in delivery of programmes central to economic development and transport objectives. Shift of West Rapid Transport from revenue to capital suggests changes in project scope or structure a lender would track.
findings.figures: Investment Fund: £29.3m budget vs £23.4m forecast (£5.9m reduction, 20%); Spatial Development Strategy £1.8m; West Rapid Transport £1.5m
findings.quote: The Q1 forecast shows a reduction in expenditure of £5.9m (20%) against the current budget (£29.3m vs £23.4m). This reduction primarily reflects the reprofiling of projects into later years as delivery plans have been updated.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 09 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast
findings.headline: Capital Programme historical underdelivery averaging 11.4% below Q1 forecast over two years; Optimism Bias Factor reduced from £82.5m (26%) to £33.8m based on actual performance
findings.detail: Budget was set with Optimism Bias Factor of £82.5m (26% of gross delivery expenditure). Analysis of actual capital outturn over last two years shows delivery fell average 11.4% below Q1 forecast. Authority has therefore applied more conservative allowance of £33.8m (11.4% of current forecast) to reflect actual delivery patterns.
findings.matters: Significant reduction in Optimism Bias and evidence of consistent underdelivery indicates systemic issues with capital programme forecasting and execution. Relevant to a lender assessing reliability of capital delivery commitments and cash flow forecasts.
findings.figures: Original Optimism Bias: £82.5m (26% of gross); Applied factor: £33.8m (11.4% of gross); historical underdelivery 11.4% average over two years
findings.quote: The budget was set with an Optimism Bias Factor of £82.5m, equivalent to 26% of gross delivery expenditure. Actual capital outturn over the last two years has fallen an average of 11.4% below the Q1 forecast, and the forecast therefore applies an allowance of £33.8m

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 09 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast
findings.headline: Employee costs £2.1m (7%) below budget due to slower-than-anticipated recruitment across delivery (£1.9m) and corporate (£0.2m) areas, with posts held pending Target Operating Model finalisation
findings.detail: Employee costs forecast £28.5m against budget £30.6m, creating £2.1m underspend. Of this, £1.9m relates to slower recruitment in delivery areas and £0.2m in corporate areas. Authority attributes this to wider public sector recruitment challenges and difficulty phasing organisational growth at budget setting. Target Operating Model development is also influencing timing of appointments. Posts are being held rather than removed.
findings.matters: Recruitment delays mask budget underspends but indicate operational challenges and service capacity uncertainty. Dependency on TOM finalisation for recruitment decisions shows strategic planning uncertainty.
findings.figures: Employee costs: £30.6m budget vs £28.5m forecast (£2.1m underspend); Delivery underspend £1.9m; Corporate underspend £0.2m
findings.quote: Employee costs are currently forecast to come in £2.1m (7%), lower than budget. £1.9m of the variance relates to slower than anticipated recruitment in the delivery areas, with a further £0.2m relating to recruitment delays across the corporate areas

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 09 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast
findings.headline: Grant funding £6.0m (6%) below budget, with Investment Fund reduced £5.9m due to project reprofiling into later years
findings.detail: Total grant funding forecast at £87.4m against budget £93.4m (£6.0m reduction, 6%). Of this, £5.9m is attributable to Investment Fund reprofiling of projects into later years. Spatial Development Strategy and West Rapid Transport account for £1.8m and £1.5m of variance respectively.
findings.matters: Reduction in grant income indicates either lower funding awards or timing mismatches affecting delivery. Reprofiling also signals delivery delays extending beyond current year.
findings.figures: Grant funding: £93.4m budget vs £87.4m forecast (£6.0m reduction); Investment Fund: £29.3m vs £23.4m (£5.9m reduction); Spatial Development Strategy £1.8m; West Rapid Transport £1.5m
findings.quote: Grant funding remains the largest source of income at £87.4m, though this is £6.0m (6%) below the current budget. The main movements include (£5.9m) relates to the Investment Fund.

findings.committee: Joint meeting - West of England Combined Authority Committee and West of England Joint Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 09 - MCA and Mayoral Budget Forecast
findings.headline: Multiple major capital transport schemes delayed: Getting Around Yate & Thornbury (6 months, £3.5m), Alveston Hill (on hold, planning, £1.8m), A4 Portway (redesign, £1.4m), Bedminster Bridges (FBC approval, £1.2m)
findings.detail: Four major transport capital projects experiencing significant delays. Getting Around Yate and Thornbury has six-month construction delay (£3.5m variance). Alveston Hill on hold due to planning issues with estimated six-month delay (£1.8m). A4 Portway delayed by redesign work (£1.4m). Bedminster Bridges delayed by FBC approval processes (£1.2m). These delays affect delivery timelines and funding profiles.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess delivery risk and whether schemes will consume funding as planned. Repeated delays on major corridor and infrastructure projects may indicate systemic programme management challenges.
findings.figures: Yate & Thornbury £3.5m (6-month delay); Alveston Hill £1.8m (on hold); A4 Portway £1.4m; Bedminster Bridges £1.2m
findings.quote: The Getting Around Yate and Thornbury project has experienced a six-month delay to construction, resulting in a £3.5m reduction in forecast expenditure. The Alveston Hill project is currently on hold due to planning issues, with an estimated six-month delay
